title: Talha ibn Ubayd Allah
content:

[[Rashidun Caliphate]] (632–656) | battles = {{tree list}} *Under [[Muhammad]] **[[Battle of Uhud]] **[[Battle of Hamra al-Asad]] **[[Expedition of Dhu Qarad]] **[[Invasion of Banu Qaynuqa]] **[[Invasion of Banu Nadir]] **[[Expedition of Badr al-Maw'id]] **[[Expedition of Dhat al-Riqa]] **[[Expedition of Dumat al-Jandal]] **[[Expedition of al-Muraysi']] **[[Battle of the Trench]] **[[Invasion of Banu Qurayza]] **[[Invasion of Banu Lahyan]] **[[Expedition of Dhu Qarad]] **[[Conquest of Fadak]] **[[Battle of Khaybar]] **[[Third Expedition of Wadi al Qura]] **[[Conquest of Mecca]] **[[Battle of Hunayn]] **[[Battle of Autas]] **[[Siege of Ta'if]] **[[Expedition of Tabuk|Battle of Tabuk]] *[[Ridda Wars]] **[[Battle of Dhu al-Qassah]] *[[Early Muslim conquests]] *[[First Fitna]] **[[Battle of the Camel]]{{KIA}} {{tree list/end}} }} '''Talha ibn Ubayd Allah al-Taymi''' ({{langx|ar|طَلْحَة بن عُبَيْد اللّه التَّيمي|Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Taymī}}), {{circa|594|656}}) was a companion of the Islamic prophet [[Muhammad]]. In [[Sunni Islam]], he is known for being among {{transliteration|ar|[[The ten to whom Paradise was promised|al-ʿashara al-mubashshara]]}} ('the ten to whom Paradise was promised')[http://sunnah.com/abudawud/42/54 Abu Dawud 41:4632.] and was given the title "the Generous" by Muhammad.[http://library.islamweb.net/newlibrary/display_book.php?ID=2&bk_no=60&flag=1 سير أعلام النبلاء، لشمس الدين الذهبي، ترجمة طلحة بن عبيد الله، الجزء الأول، صـ 24: 40] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171218173352/http://library.islamweb.net/newlibrary/display_book.php?ID=2&bk_no=60&flag=1 |date=18 December 2017}} Talha played significant roles in the [[Battle of Uhud]] and the [[Battle of the Camel]], where he was killed. He is viewed critically in Shia Islam due to his role in the [[First Fitna]]. == Ancestry and early life == Talha was born c. 594,Muhammad ibn Saad. ''Kitab al-Tabaqat al-Kabir'' vol. 3. Translated by Bewley, A. (2013. ''The Companions of Badr''. London: Ta-Ha Publishers. A member of the [[Banu Taym|Taym]] clan of the Quraysh in [[Mecca]], Talha was the son of Ubayd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Amr ibn Ka'b ibn Sa'd ibn Taym ibn Murra ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ay ibn Ghalib and of al-Sa'ba bint Abd Allah, who was from the Hadram tribe. Talha's lineage meets with that of Muhammad at [[Murra ibn Ka'b]]. == Career during Muhammad's era (610–632) == === Conversion and persecution in Mecca === [[Muhammad Marmaduke Pickthall]] describes how [[Abu Bakr]], after embracing Islam, immediately urged his closest associates to do likewise. Among them were Talha, [[Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf]], [[Uthman|Uthman ibn Affan]], and [[Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas]].{{cite book |author1=Marmaduke Pickthall |author2=Muhammad Asad |author1-link=Marmaduke Pickthall |title=Islamic Culture Volume 53 |date=1979|type=zation, Islamic -- Periodicals, Civilization, Mohammedan, Islam -- Periodicals, Islamic civilization -- Periodicals, Islamic countries -- Civilization, Islamic countries -- Civilization -- Periodicals, Mohammedanism -- Periodical |publisher=Islamic Culture Boards; Academic and Cultural Publications Charitable Trust |location=Hydebarad, India |page=152 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=q4BCAAAAYAAJ |access-date=13 March 2022 |language=en}} Talha is said to have been among the first eight converts.Muhammad ibn Ishaq. ''Sirat Rasul Allah''. Translated by Guillaume, A. (1955). ''The Life of Muhammad''. Oxford: Oxford University Press.{{rp|115}}{{rp|164}} Among the converts in Mecca, Talha shared responsibility as a [[Hafiz (Quran)|hafiz]], people who memorized every verse of the Quran, along with Abu Bakr, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, [[Zubayr ibn al-Awwam]] and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.{{sfn|Abdullah|Abdullah|Rosman|Ilias|2016|p=43. quoting al-Azami, 2005; Ahmad Don, 1991; al-Zarqani, t.th}} During the persecution of the Muslims in 614–616, [[Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid]] tied Talha to Abu Bakr and left them bound together. Nobody from the Taym clan came to help.{{rp|164}} Thereafter they became known as "the Two Tied Together".{{rp|127–128,337}} === Migration to Medina === In September 622, while returning from a business trip to Syria, Talha encountered Muslims who had left Mecca and were [[Hegira|emigrating]] to [[Medina]].{{cite book |author1=Muhammad Yasin Mazhar Siddiqi |title=The Prophet Muhammad A Role Model for Muslim Minorities |date=2016|type=Biography & Autobiography / Religious, Religion / Islam / General, Religion / Islam / History, Social Science / Islamic Studies, Muhammad, Prophet, -632, Muslims, Muslims -- Non-Islamic countries -- Religious life |publisher=Kube Publishing Limited |isbn=9780860376774 |page=103 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=47hoDQAAQBAJ |access-date=13 March 2022 |language=en |format=ebook}} Talha gave them Syrian garments and mentioned that the Muslim community in Medina had said that their prophet was slow to arrive. As Muhammad and Abu Bakr continued to Medina, Talha returned to Mecca to put his affairs in order. Soon afterwards, he accompanied Abu Bakr's family to Medina, where he settled.{{rp|164}} === Military Career (624–632) === At first he lodged with [[As'ad ibn Zurara]], but later Muhammad gave him a block of land on which he built his own house. He was made the brother in Islam of [[Sa'id ibn Zayd]].{{rp|165}} Talha and Sa'id missed fighting at the [[Battle of Badr]] because Muhammad sent them as scouts to locate [[Abu Sufyan ibn Harb|Abu Sufyan's]] caravan. However, both were awarded shares of the plunder, as if they had been present.{{rp|165}} Talha distinguished himself at the [[Battle of Uhud]] by keeping close to Muhammad while most of the Muslim army fled. He protected Muhammad's face from an arrow by taking the blow with his own hand, resulting in the loss of his index and middle fingers. He was also struck twice in the head, and it was said that he suffered a total of 39 or 75{{rp|165–166}} wounds. Toward the end of the battle, Talha fainted from his heavy injuries,{{Cite wikisource | title = البداية والنهاية/الجزء الرابع/فصل فيما لقي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يومئذ من المشركين قبحهم الله | last = Ibn Kathir | first = Ismail }} The Beginning and the End, by Ibn Kathir al-Dimashqi, Part IV, Chapter: What the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, met on that day from the polytheists, may God vilify them Abu Bakr soon reached their location to check Muhammad's condition first, who immediately instructed Abu Bakr to check the condition of Talha, who had already passed out due to his severe blood loss{{cite book |author1=Afzal Hoosen Elias |title=The Lives of the Sahabah |date=2008|type=Religion / Islam / General |publisher=Dar al-Kotob Ilmiyah |page=491 |isbn=9782745159342 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ui1uDwAAQBAJ |access-date=13 March 2022 |language=en}} and his hand was left paralysed. For this heroic defence of Muhammad, Talha earned the byname "the living martyr".{{cite book |author1=Safiur Rahman Mubarakpuri |editor1-last=Nayra |translator=Abu Ahsan |editor1-first=Abu |title=Periode Madinah; Aktivitas Militer Menjelang Perang Uhud dan Perang Ahzab |trans-title= Medina period: military activity on the eve of battle of Uhud & Ahzab |date=2021|type=Religion / General, Religion / Islam / General, Religion / Islam / History, Religion / Reference |publisher=Hikam Pustaka |isbn=9786233114158 |pages=78–79 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BWhgEAAAQBAJ |access-date=12 March 2022 |language=id |format=ebook}} Talha is said to be the anonymous believer counted as a "martyr" in {{Cite quran|33|23|s=r|t=s}}.{{cite book |author1=Ahmad Salah |title=في حب الصحابة|trans-title=In love with the Companions |date=2009|type=Religion / Islam / General |publisher=Dar Annashr For Universit |isbn=9796500050379 |page=260 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fKrEDgAAQBAJ |access-date=12 March 2022 |language=ar}} Abu Bakr also called the Battle of Uhud "the day of Talha". Talha fought at the [[Battle of the Trench]] and all the [[List of expeditions of Muhammad|campaigns of Muhammad]].{{rp|166}} During the [[Expedition of Dhu Qarad]], Talha personally sponsored the operation through his wealth, thus causing Muhammad to give him the sobriquet "Talha al-Fayyad".{{cite book |author1=Muhammad Al-Said bin Bassiouni Zaghloul |title=الموسوعة الكبرى لأطراف الحديث النبوي الشريف 1-50 ج49|trans-title=The Great Encyclopedia of Extremities of the Noble Hadith 1-50 C 49 |date=2021|type=Literary Criticism / Subjects & Themes / General |publisher=Dar al Kotob Ilmiyah |page=515 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LH1JEAAAQBAJ |access-date=12 March 2022 |language=ar |format=ebook}} == Career during the Rashidun Caliphate (632–656) == === Defense of Medina and the Ridda Wars === {{Main|Ridda Wars#Battle of Dhu al-Qassah}} In the third week of July 632, Medina faced an imminent invasion by the [[Ridda wars|apostate forces]] of [[Tulayha]], a self-proclaimed prophet. Abu Bakr immediately formed organised elite guard units [[Haras (unit)|al-Ḥaras wa al-Shurṭa]] to defend Medina, appointing Talha, [[Ali ibn Abi Talib]] and Zubayr each overseeing roughly one-third of the newly organised force.{{cite book|last1=Ibn Jarir at-Tabari|first1=Muhammad|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MP_oI6wuyOcC|title=The History of Al-Tabari Vol. 10 The Conquest of Arabia: The Riddah Wars A.D. 632-633/A.H. 11|date=June 15, 2015|publisher=State University of New York Press|isbn=9781438401409|edition=Fred Donner Translation|page=46|access-date=14 October 2021}} === Strategic Counsel and the Shura Council === {{Main|Majlis al-Shura}} {{See also|Battle of al-Qadisiyyah|Battle of Nahavand}} Throughout the Rashidun era, Talha served as a high-ranking member of the [[Majlis al-Shura]] (Consultative Council). In 635 to 636, Caliph [[Umar]] assembled the council to deliberate on the battle plan for facing the Sasanian army at Qadisiyyah.{{cite web |title=معركة القادسية|trans-title= The story of Arab civilization in one digital library; Battle of Qadisiyyah |url=http://al-hakawati.net/Cultures/CultureDetails/169/%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%B1%D9%83%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9 |website=2022 © Al-Hakawati - Arab Foundation for Culture |issn=2379-7290 |access-date=2 January 2022}} While Umar initially intended to lead the army himself, Talha and the other senior advisors urged him to remain in the capital for administrative stability, resulting in the appointment of [[Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas]] as the supreme commander. Later, upon hearing that Sasanian forces from Mah, [[Qom]], [[Hamadan]], [[Ray, Iran|Ray]], [[Isfahan]], [[Azerbaijan]], and [[Nahavand]] had gathered to counter the Muslim invasion, Umar assembled a war council consisting of Talha, Zubayr, Ali, Uthman, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and [[Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib]].{{cite book |last1=bin Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Hayyan |first1=Abi Muhammad Abdullah |editor1-last=Abdul-Haq Al-Hussein Al-Balushi |editor1-first=Abdul-Ghafoor |title=طبقات المحدثين بأصبهان والواردين عليها - ج ١|trans-title=The layers of the modernists in Isfahan and those who received it - Part 1 |date=1991 |publisher=al-Risalah foundation publishing, printing, and distribution |page=195 |url=https://books.rafed.net/m/?type=c_fbook&b_id=2428&page=195 |access-date=20 December 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Sirjani |first1=Raghib |author1-link=Ragheb Sergani |title=the dismissal of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas |url=https://islamstory.com/ar/artical/19906/%D8%B9%D8%B2%D9%84_%D8%B3%D9%80%D8%B9%D8%AF_%D8%A8%D9%86_%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%89_%D9%88%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%B5 |website=Islamstory.com |access-date=19 December 2021 |language=ar|date=2006}} Following the advice of Ali to delegate command rather than leading the expedition himself, Umar appointed [[Al-Nu'man ibn Muqrin]] to lead the main force to Nahavand, with reinforcement commands delegated to Zubayr, Tulayha, [[Amr ibn Ma'adi Yakrib]], and others.{{cite book |last1=bin Shamil as-sulami |first1=Muhammad |translator=Abu Ihsan al-Atsari |editor1-last=Amin Sjihab |editor1-first=Ahmad |title=Tartib wa Tahdzib Al-Kkitab bidayah wan Nihayah by Ibn Kathir |date=2004 |publisher=Dar al-Wathan Riyadh KSA ; DARUL HAQ, Jakarta |location=Jakarta |pages=218–220 |url=https://adoc.pub/judul-asli-tartib-wa-tahdzib-al-kkitab-bidayah-wan-nihayah-p.html |access-date=22 December 2021 |language=id, ar}}{{cite book |last1=Abd al Hadi |first1=Ahmad |title=من معارك الفتوح الإسلامية |trans-title=From the battles of the Islamic conquests |isbn= 9789775967466|publisher= مركز الراية للنشر والإعلام،|date=2001 |page=120 |access-date=6 December 2021 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=k8FtAAAAMAAJ&q=%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9%20%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B2%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%B1%20%D8%A8%D9%86%20%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%85|language=ar}} === Death at the Battle of the Camel === {{Main|First Fitna#Battle of the Camel}} [[File:Tomb of Talha.jpg|thumb|right|Tomb of Talha ibn Ubayd Allah at Basra, Iraq]] Talha was killed at the [[Battle of the Camel]] on 10 December 656. Several conflicting narratives have been provided to explain how it happened. According to one account, during the battle, [[Marwan ibn al-Hakam]], who was fighting on the same side as Aisha, shot Talha in the thigh.Madelung, Wilferd (1997). ''[https://archive.org/details/TheSuccessionToMuhammadByWilferdMadelung/page/n190/mode/1up The Succession to Muhammad: A Study of the Early Caliphate]''. Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|978-0521646963}} Another account attributes Talha's death to being killed by Ali's supporters while retreating from the field.{{sfn|Landau-Tasseron|1998|pp=27–28, note 126}} Talha hugged his horse and galloped off the battlefield. He lay down using a stone as a pillow, while the auxiliaries tried to staunch the blood flow. Whenever they stopped pressing, the bleeding resumed. In the end, Talha said, "Stop it. This is an arrow sent by [[God in Islam|God]]." He died of this injury, aged 64.{{rp|170–171}} == Personal life == === Characteristics === Talha was described as a brown-skinned man with a great deal of wavy hair, a handsome face and a narrow nose. He liked to wear saffron-dyed clothes and musk. He walked swiftly and, when nervous, he would toy with his ring, which was of gold and set with a ruby.{{rp|167–168}} === Family === Talha had at least fifteen children by at least 12 different women.Muhammad ibn Saad. ''Kitab al-Tabaqat al-Kabir'' vol. 8. Translated by Bewley, A. (1995). ''The Women of Madina''. London: Ta-Ha Publishers: The known descendants of Talha by his various wives and concubines have divided into six lines.{{harvnb|Q. Ahmed|2011|pp=81–105}} === Wealth === Talha was a successful cloth merchant who eventually left an estate estimated at 30 million dirhams.{{rp|153,169-1670}} According to modern writer Asad Ahmed, his wealth was second only to that of Uthman ibn Affan. He owned property in Iraq that reportedly yielded four to five hundred dinars in gold, and initiated agricultural ventures such as ''al-Qumh'' (wheat) cultivation for his community. Talha is said to have amassed much of his fortune by exchanging properties acquired from the [[Battle of Khaybar]] for lands in Iraq held by Arab Hejazi settlers, and through transactions of several estates in [[Hadhramaut]] with Uthman. He also profited from trade throughout Syria and Yemen during his lifetime. == Tomb == {{main|Mausoleum of Talha ibn 'Ubayd Allah}} Talha ibn 'Ubayd Allah is buried in [[Basra]], [[Iraq]] in a mausoleum which is currently under construction as of 2025. The mausoleum was formerly part of a 1973 mosque complex that was destroyed by explosives in a revenge attack by [[Shi'ite]] militias for the [[2006 al-Askari mosque bombing]].{{Cite news extract: Talha ibn Ubayd Allah al-Taymi (Arabic: طَلْحَة بن عُبَيْد اللّه التَّيمي, romanized: Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Taymī), c. 594 – c. 656) was a companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. In Sunni Islam, he is known for being among al-ʿashara al-mubashshara ('the ten to whom Paradise was promised') and was given the title "the Generous" by Muhammad. Talha played significant roles in the Battle of Uhud and the Battle of the Camel, where he was killed. He is viewed critically in Shia Islam due to his role in the First Fitna.
